hop_dnsbl_sender_ip_lookup_domains   (default: empty)


A list of DNSBL domains to query when hop_dnsbl_sender_ip_lookup
    is enabled. For example:


hop_dnsbl_sender_ip_lookup_domains = zen.spamhaus.org, bl.spamcop.net



This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_dnsbl_sender_ip_lookup_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a message due to the sender's
    IP address being listed in a DNSBL. The default is 550, indicating a permanent
    failure.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_dnsbl_sender_ip_lookup_reject_text   (default: Sender IP listed)


The text message used when rejecting a message due to the sender's
    IP address being listed in a DNSBL. The default is "Sender IP listed".


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_explicit_plugins   (default: empty)


A list of explicit plugins to load for the SMTP client. This is
    typically used for advanced features like client-side TLS negotiation or
    custom authentication mechanisms.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_explicit_tls   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will attempt to
    establish an explicit TLS (Transport Layer Security) connection with the
    remote server before sending any mail. This provides an additional layer of
    security for email transmission.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_explicit_tls_cert_file   (default: empty)


The file path to the certificate file used for explicit TLS
    connections. This is typically used when the server needs to present a
    client certificate to the remote server for authentication.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_explicit_tls_key_file   (default: empty)


The file path to the private key file used for explicit TLS
    connections. This key corresponds to the certificate specified in
    hop_explicit_tls_cert_file.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_explicit_tls_security_level   (default: may)


The security level for explicit TLS connections. Possible values are:
    none (no TLS), may (TLS is
    optional), encrypt (TLS is required),
    verify (TLS is required and the server certificate is
    verified).


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_extra_recipient_limit   (default: 20)


The maximum number of recipients Postfix will attempt to deliver to
    in a single SMTP transaction to a remote server. This is an additional limit
    beyond the default_destination_recipient_limit.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_fingerprint_lookup   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will perform reverse
    DNS lookups to obtain the hostname of the connecting client, and then perform
    another DNS lookup (fingerprint lookup) on that hostname. This can be used
    to identify known mail servers or to apply specific policies based on the
    server's identity.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_fingerprint_lookup_domains   (default: empty)


A list of domains to query for fingerprint lookups when
    hop_fingerprint_lookup is enabled.
    For example:


hop_fingerprint_lookup_domains = servers.example.com, known_mail.net



This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_fingerprint_lookup_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a message due to a failed
    fingerprint lookup. The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_fingerprint_lookup_reject_text   (default: Unknown mail server)


The text message used when rejecting a message due to a failed
    fingerprint lookup. The default is "Unknown mail server".


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_fingerprint_lookup_send_text   (default: empty)


Text to be sent to the remote server during a fingerprint lookup.
    This is typically used to provide additional information or context to the
    lookup process.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_fingerprint_lookup_verify_host   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will verify that
    the hostname obtained from the reverse DNS lookup matches the hostname
    returned by the forward DNS lookup of the IP address. This adds an extra layer
    of verification to prevent IP spoofing.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_from_header_checks   (default: empty)


A lookup table for header checks specifically applied to the "From:"
    header of outgoing mail. This can be used to enforce sender policies or to
    detect forged sender addresses.


The format is similar to header_from_checks.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_from_header_checks_verbose   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will log detailed
    information about the matching process for
    hop_from_header_checks. This can be
    useful for debugging.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_host_lookup   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will perform a
    reverse DNS lookup to obtain the hostname of the connecting client. This
    information can be used for logging, filtering, or other policy decisions.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_over_connect_timeout   (default: 0s)


The time limit for Postfix to complete the connection establishment
    after the initial connection has been made. This includes operations like
    greeting exchange and TLS negotiation. If the process exceeds this limit,
    the delivery will be deferred. A value of 0s means no timeout.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_over_verify_recipient_timeout   (default: 0s)


The time limit for Postfix to complete recipient verification after the
    initial connection and greeting. If recipient verification exceeds this time,
    the delivery will be deferred. A value of 0s means no timeout.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_over_verify_sender_timeout   (default: 0s)


The time limit for Postfix to complete sender verification after the
    initial connection and greeting. If sender verification exceeds this time,
    the delivery will be deferred. A value of 0s means no timeout.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_pipe_timeout   (default: 10s)


The time limit for Postfix to execute a command via the pipe(8)
    delivery agent. If the command does not complete within this time, it will be
    terminated, and the delivery will be deferred.


This parameter affects the pipe(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_rcpt_to_timeout   (default: 1000s)


The time limit for Postfix to accept recipients during the SMTP
    transaction. If the server does not respond within this time, the connection
    will be closed, and the delivery will be deferred.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a message during the hop
    process (e.g., due to policy violations or failed lookups). The default is
    550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_reject_text   (default: Access denied)


The text message used when rejecting a message during the hop
    process. The default is "Access denied".


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_sender_timeout   (default: 1000s)


The time limit for Postfix to accept the sender address during the
    SMTP transaction. If the server does not respond within this time, the
    connection will be closed, and the delivery will be deferred.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_server_lookup   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will perform a
    forward DNS lookup to obtain the IP address of the remote server. This is
    typically used to verify the server's identity or to apply policies based on
    its IP address.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_smtp_session_timeout   (default: 600s)


The maximum duration of an SMTP session. If the session exceeds this
    time limit, Postfix will terminate the connection. This helps prevent
    resource exhaustion caused by long-running or stalled sessions.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






hop_tls_security_level   (default: may)


The security level for TLS (Transport Layer Security) connections
    during mail transfer. Possible values are:
    none (no TLS), may (TLS is
    optional), encrypt (TLS is required),
    verify (TLS is required and the server certificate is
    verified).


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_verify_recipient_timeout   (default: 1000s)


The time limit for Postfix to complete recipient verification with
    the remote server. If verification takes longer than this, the delivery is
    deferred.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






hop_verify_sender_timeout   (default: 1000s)


The time limit for Postfix to complete sender verification with the
    remote server. If verification takes longer than this, the delivery is
    deferred.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






home_mailbox   (default: Maildir/)


The default mailbox directory for local delivery. This parameter
    specifies the path relative to the user's home directory where mail will be
    stored. Common values include:


    
  
  • Maildir/: Stores mail in the Maildir format, which
      is recommended for its robustness and support for multiple mail clients.
      This is the default.
    • 
  
  • mbox: Stores mail in the traditional mbox format.
    • 
  
  • An absolute path: e.g., /var/mail/vhosts/user.
    • 



This parameter affects the local(8)
    and virtual(8) delivery agents.






host_name   (default: empty)


The explicit hostname to be used in Postfix-generated mail headers,
    such as the Received: header. If this parameter is
    empty, Postfix will attempt to determine the hostname from the system.


Setting this parameter is useful for ensuring consistent hostname
    information across multiple servers or in environments where the system
    hostname may not be fully qualified or reliable.






html_output_encoding   (default: utf-8)


The character encoding to use when generating HTML output for email
    messages. The default is UTF-8, which supports a wide range of characters.
    Other encodings may be specified if needed.


This parameter affects the MIME generation process.






ignore_header_newlines   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will ignore newlines
    within email header fields. This allows for long header lines to be folded
    across multiple lines without being treated as separate headers. This is the
    standard behavior according to RFC standards.


If disabled (no), Postfix will treat each
    line with a newline as a separate header field, which can lead to unexpected
    behavior or message rejection.






impersonate_local_domain   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will append the
    local domain name to sender addresses that do not have a domain specified.
    This is a security measure to prevent spoofing by ensuring that all sender
    addresses have a fully qualified domain name.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






injected_content_filter   (default: empty)


Specifies a content filter that is applied to mail injected directly
    into Postfix (e.g., via the sendmail command or the LMTP client). This allows
    for content scanning and manipulation of locally generated mail before it is
    queued for delivery.


The value is a lookup table, similar to
    content_filter_table.


This parameter affects mail injected via the sendmail command and
    other local submission methods.






input_queue_depth_limit   (default: 1000)


The maximum number of messages that can be queued for input processing
    by the smtpd(8) server. This limits the
    number of concurrent incoming connections and helps prevent resource
    exhaustion.






input_queue_filter   (default: empty)


Specifies a filter that is applied to messages as they are received
    by the smtpd(8) server. This can be used
    for pre-queue filtering based on various criteria.


The value is a lookup table, similar to
    header_checks or
    body_checks.






input_queue_filter_verbose   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will log detailed
    information about the matching process for
    input_queue_filter. This can be useful for
    debugging.






input_throttle_delay   (default: 0s)


The delay introduced between accepting incoming connections by the
    smtpd(8) server. A non-zero value can be
    used to rate-limit incoming mail and protect against DoS attacks.


Specify a time value (e.g., 1s, 5m, 1h).






internal_das_loops   (default: 5)


The maximum number of times Postfix will retry a delivery to the same
    destination within a short period if it encounters temporary errors. This is
    part of Postfix's adaptive delivery scheduling mechanism.






internal_das_loops_max_count   (default: 100)


The maximum number of deliveries Postfix will attempt to the same
    destination before giving up, even if temporary errors persist. This prevents
    infinite retries for undeliverable mail.






internal_das_loops_max_time   (default: 1d)


The maximum time Postfix will continue retrying deliveries to the
    same destination when temporary errors occur. After this period, the message
    will be deferred for a longer duration or returned as undeliverable.


The time unit can be s (seconds), m (minutes), h (hours), d
    (days), w (weeks).






internal_das_loops_retry_interval   (default: 10m)


The interval between retries for deliveries that have encountered
    temporary errors. This parameter controls how frequently Postfix re-attempts
    delivery after a failure.


The time unit can be s (seconds), m (minutes), h (hours), d
    (days), w (weeks).






internal_mailbox_limit   (default: auto)


The maximum size of a mailbox for local delivery. If a mailbox exceeds
    this limit, new mail may be rejected or deferred. The default value 'auto'
    adjusts the limit based on system resources.


This parameter affects the local(8)
    and virtual(8) delivery agents.






internal_mail_filter   (default: empty)


Specifies a filter that is applied to mail delivered locally by Postfix.
    This allows for content scanning or modification of mail before it reaches the
    user's mailbox.


The value is a lookup table, similar to
    content_filter_table.


This parameter affects the local(8)
    and virtual(8) delivery agents.






internal_mail_filter_verbose   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will log detailed
    information about the matching process for
    internal_mail_filter. This can be useful
    for debugging.






keep_since_in_body   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will preserve the
    "Since" header in the body of messages when performing certain transformations.
    This is typically used in conjunction with specific content filtering or
    modification scenarios.






local_address_maps   (default: empty)


A list of lookup tables that map external addresses to internal
    recipient addresses for local delivery. This is often used in conjunction
    with virtual domains or shared mailboxes.


Example:
    hash:/etc/postfix/local_address
    Where /etc/postfix/local_address might contain:
    external@example.com   internal_user


This parameter affects the local(8)
    and virtual(8) delivery agents.






local_bounce_destination_recipient_limit   (default: 1)


The maximum number of recipients for bounce messages generated by
    local delivery. By default, bounce messages are sent to only one recipient
    (typically the postmaster) to avoid mail loops.


This parameter affects the local(8)
    delivery agent.






local_delivery_status_filter   (default: empty)


Specifies a filter for the delivery status text generated by the
    local delivery agent. This can be used to modify or censor the status
    information reported to the sender, for example, to hide specific delivery
    details.


The value is a lookup table, where each entry consists of a regular
    expression and a replacement string.


Example:


/etc/postfix/local_dsn_filter:
    /^(2\S+ delivered to file).+/    $1
    /^(2\S+ delivered to command).+/ $1



This feature will NOT override the soft_bounce
    safety net. It will change the enhanced status code and text that is logged
    to the maillog file, and that is reported to the sender in delivery
    confirmation or non-delivery notifications.


This feature is available in Postfix 3.0 and later.






local_domain_maps   (default: empty)


A list of lookup tables that define additional local domains for which
    this machine is the final destination. This is an alternative or supplement to
    the destinations parameter.


Example:
    hash:/etc/postfix/local_domains
    Where /etc/postfix/local_domains might contain:
    example.net   OK


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






local_lmtp_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a message during local LMTP
    delivery. The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the lmtp(8)
    delivery agent.






local_master_service_list   (default: local,virtual)


A comma-separated list of master service names that are considered
    local delivery agents. This parameter is used internally by Postfix to
    determine which services handle local mail delivery.






local_recipient_maps   (default: proxy:unix:passwd.byname,$myname)


A list of lookup tables that Postfix consults to determine if a
    recipient address is local. Postfix queries these tables in the order they
    are listed.


The default value includes:


    
  
  • proxy:unix:passwd.byname: Uses the system's user
      database (via the proxy service) to look up user accounts.
    • 
  
  • $myname: Checks if the recipient address matches the
      system's hostname.
    • 



Additional tables, such as virtual alias maps or hash files, can be
    added to this list.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server and the local(8) delivery agent.






local(8)
    delivery agent.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server and the queue manager.






lock_environment   (default: empty)


A list of environment variables that should be inherited by Postfix
    child processes when acquiring locks. This is typically used for security
    purposes to ensure that sensitive environment variables are not passed to
    untrusted processes.






lock_file_owner   (default: postfix)


The owner of the lock files created by Postfix. This is typically set
    to the user that the Postfix daemons run as (usually 'postfix'). This ensures
    proper file permissions and security.






lock_file_permissions   (default: 0600)


The permissions of the lock files created by Postfix. The default
    (0600) allows only the owner to read and write the file, which is a secure
    setting.






log_destination   (default: maillog)


The destination for Postfix log messages. This can be a file (e.g.,
    maillog), syslog, or other destinations supported by
    the system's logging facility.


The default value maillog directs logs to the
    system's mail log file (often `/var/log/maillog` or `/var/log/mail.log`).






log_facility   (default: mail)


The syslog facility to use for logging Postfix messages. The default
    is mail, which is the standard facility for mail
    system logging.






log_level   (default: 0)


The logging level for Postfix messages. Higher values indicate more
    detailed logging. The default level (0) provides a moderate level of logging.
    Setting this to a higher value (e.g., 1, 2, or 3) can be useful for
    troubleshooting.






log_name   (default: postfix)


The name that Postfix uses in log messages. The default is
    postfix. This allows administrators to easily identify
    Postfix-related log entries.






main_log_verbose   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will log additional
    information about the main configuration file processing. This can be useful
    for debugging configuration loading issues.






master_service_list   (default: smtp,bounce,anvil,defer,discard,error,flush,local,pipe,proxymap,relay,retry,scache,sendmail,virtual)


A comma-separated list of Postfix master service names that are
    actively running or available for use. This parameter is used internally by
    Postfix for various management and monitoring tasks.






mailbox_size_limit   (default: 0)


The maximum size (in bytes) of a user's mailbox. If a mailbox exceeds
    this limit, new mail will be deferred or rejected. A value of 0 means no
    limit (or the limit is determined by the operating system or filesystem).


This parameter affects the local(8)
    and virtual(8) delivery agents.






mail_name   (default: $myhostname)


The name of the mail system, used in the Date:
    and Message-ID: headers. By default, it is set to the
    system's fully qualified domain name ($myhostname).






mail_owner   (default: postfix)


The system user that owns the mail system files and processes. This is
    typically set to the user Postfix runs as (e.g., 'postfix').






mail_spool_directory   (default: /var/mail)


The directory where local mailboxes are stored. This is the parent
    directory for mailboxes specified by home_mailbox.






mail_version   (default: Postfix)


The string used in the X-Mailer: or similar
    headers to identify the mail software. The default is "Postfix".






mailbox_command   (default: empty)


A command to be executed to deliver mail to a user's mailbox. This
    is typically used when the standard local(8)
    delivery agent is not sufficient, for example, when using a custom mailbox
    format or delivering to a remote storage system.


The command is executed with the message piped to its standard
    input. Placeholders like %u (username) and
    %d (domain) can be used.


Example:
    mailbox_command = /usr/bin/deliver-mail %u


This parameter affects the local(8)
    and virtual(8) delivery agents.






mailbox_transport   (default: local:$)'


The default message delivery transport for mail delivered to mailboxes.
    This parameter specifies the entry in the master.cf file that Postfix should
    use. The default is the local(8) delivery
    agent.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server and the queue manager.






mailbox_virtual_transport   (default: virtual:$)'


The default message delivery transport for mail delivered to virtual
    mailboxes. This parameter specifies the entry in the master.cf file that
    Postfix should use. The default is the virtual(8)
    delivery agent.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server and the queue manager.






max_idle_time   (default: 1000s)


The maximum time a Postfix daemon process will remain idle before
    exiting. This helps to manage system resources by terminating unused
    processes. The time unit can be s (seconds), m (minutes), h (hours), d
    (days), w (weeks).






max_jobs   (default: 10000)


The maximum number of messages that can be simultaneously in the Postfix
    queue. This limits the total size of the queue and helps prevent disk space
    exhaustion.






max_use   (default: 100000)


The maximum number of times a Postfix daemon process will be reused
    before it is replaced. This helps to prevent resource leaks or memory
    fragmentation that might occur over long periods of operation.






message_body_delimiter   (default: empty)


A string that is used to separate the header from the body of a
    message. By default, this is an empty string, meaning that Postfix assumes
    the standard CRLF pair as the delimiter. This parameter is rarely changed.






message_deadline   (default: 10d)


The maximum time a message can remain in the Postfix queue before it
    is considered undeliverable and returned to the sender with a bounce
    message. The default is 10 days. The time unit can be s (seconds), m
    (minutes), h (hours), d (days), w (weeks).






message_size_limit   (default: 10240000)


The maximum size (in bytes) of an entire email message, including
    headers and body. Messages exceeding this limit will be rejected. The default
    is 10 MB.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






message_timestamp_format   (default: $date_format)


The format string used for timestamps in Postfix log messages. By
    default, it uses the system's date format settings.






message_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting an entire message based on
    its size or other message-level criteria. The default is 550, indicating a
    permanent failure.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






message_reject_text   (default: Message exceeds)


The text message used when rejecting an entire message. This text is
    appended to the rejection code (e.g., "Message exceeds maximum size").


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






mime_header_folding_width   (default: 76)


The maximum width (in characters) for folding MIME header lines. This
    parameter controls how long header lines are wrapped to fit within the
    specified width. The default is 76 characters, a common standard.






mime_types   (default: empty)


A lookup table that defines MIME types for different file extensions.
    This is used by Postfix when generating MIME-encoded messages, such as
    multipart messages or attachments.


Example:
    text/html    html htm
    application/pdf  pdf






milter_connect_argument_macros   (default: i)


Specifies which macros should be passed to the milter's
    connect callback. The default value 'i' means the
    client IP address is passed.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_connect_macros   (default: i)


Specifies which macros should be passed to the milter's
    connect callback. The default value 'i' means the
    client IP address is passed.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_daemon_timeout   (default: 300s)


The timeout duration for communication with milter daemons. If a milter
    daemon does not respond within this time, Postfix will assume the milter is
    unavailable and may take alternative actions (e.g., reject the message or
    continue processing without the milter).


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_forbidden_macros   (default: empty)


A list of macros that should NOT be passed to milters. This can be
    used to prevent sensitive information from being exposed to external filter
    programs.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_macro_allow_chars   (default: empty)


A list of characters that are allowed in milter macro values. This is
    used for security purposes to sanitize macro content before passing it to
    milters.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_macro_daemon_name   (default: empty)


Specifies the name of the milter daemon that should be used for
    macro processing. This is typically used in conjunction with specific milter
    configurations.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_macro_definition   (default: empty)


Allows defining custom macro names and values that can be passed to
    milters. This enables more advanced integration with external filtering
    systems.


Example:
    milter_macro_definition = _MY_VAR="some value" _ANOTHER_VAR="another value"


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_macro_lookup_table   (default: empty)


Specifies a lookup table for defining milter macro values. This allows
    for dynamic or complex macro definitions based on external data.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_macro_send_name   (default: empty)


Specifies the name of the milter daemon to which macro information
    should be sent. This is typically used in conjunction with specific milter
    configurations.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_protocol   (default: 2)


The version of the milter protocol to use when communicating with
    milter daemons. Version 2 is the current standard and offers more features
    than version 1.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_rcpt_macros   (default: i)


Specifies which macros should be passed to the milter's
    rcptto callback. The default value 'i' means the
    client IP address is passed.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when a message is rejected by a milter. The
    default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_reject_text   (default: Access denied by filter)


The text message used when a message is rejected by a milter. The
    default is "Access denied by filter".


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_protocol_connect_argument_macros   (default: i)


Specifies which macros should be passed to the milter's
    connect callback when using protocol version 2. The
    default value 'i' means the client IP address is passed.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_protocol_connect_macros   (default: i)


Specifies which macros should be passed to the milter's
    connect callback when using protocol version 2. The
    default value 'i' means the client IP address is passed.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_protocol_rcpt_macros   (default: i)


Specifies which macros should be passed to the milter's
    rcptto callback when using protocol version 2. The
    default value 'i' means the client IP address is passed.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_server_port   (default: empty)


The TCP port number on which milter daemons listen for connections. If
    this is not specified, Postfix will attempt to use the service name defined
    in milter_service_name.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_service_name   (default: milter)


The service name used to look up the TCP port for milter daemons. If
    milter_server_port is not specified,
    Postfix will query the services database for this name.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_socket_name   (default: empty)


The path to the UNIX-domain socket used for communication with milter
    daemons. If this is specified, Postfix will use a local socket instead of a
    TCP connection.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






milter_timeout   (default: 300s)


The timeout duration for communication with milter daemons. This is a
    synonym for milter_daemon_timeout.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






missing_header_length_limit   (default: auto)


The maximum length allowed for header fields that are missing or
    incomplete. This helps prevent denial-of-service attacks by limiting the
    impact of malformed headers. The default value 'auto' adjusts the limit based
    on system resources.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






missing_header_lines_limit   (default: auto)


The maximum number of lines allowed for header fields that are missing
    or incomplete. This helps prevent denial-of-service attacks by limiting the
    impact of malformed headers. The default value 'auto' adjusts the limit based
    on system resources.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






mixed_message_header_length_limit   (default: auto)


The maximum length allowed for header fields within mixed messages
    (e.g., multipart messages). This helps prevent denial-of-service attacks by
    limiting the size of potentially complex headers. The default value 'auto'
    adjusts the limit based on system resources.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






mixed_message_header_lines_limit   (default: auto)


The maximum number of lines allowed for header fields within mixed
    messages. This helps prevent denial-of-service attacks by limiting the size
    of potentially complex headers. The default value 'auto' adjusts the limit
    based on system resources.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






mnserv_connect_timeout   (default: 30s)


The time limit for Postfix to establish a connection to a mail
    notification server. This parameter is used in conjunction with specific
    notification services.






mnserv_command_timeout   (default: 10s)


The time limit for Postfix to execute a command on a mail notification
    server. If the command does not complete within this time, it will be
    terminated.






mnserv_host_lookup   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will perform a
    reverse DNS lookup to obtain the hostname of the mail notification server.
    This information can be used for logging or policy decisions.






mnserv_message_timeout   (default: 1000s)


The time limit for Postfix to send a message to a mail notification
    server. If the server does not respond within this time, the message will be
    deferred.






mnserv_send_timeout   (default: 10s)


The time limit for Postfix to send data to a mail notification
    server. If the server does not respond within this time, the connection will
    be closed.






nntp_destination_concurrency_limit   (default: 10)


The maximum number of parallel deliveries to the NNTP service. This
    parameter is specific to the NNTP transport (if configured).






nntp_destination_recipient_limit   (default: 50)


The maximum number of recipients per message when delivering to the
    NNTP service. This parameter is specific to the NNTP transport (if
    configured).






ns_child_timeout   (default: 30s)


The time limit for a child process of the Postfix nameserver lookup
    utility (dns(8)) to complete its task. If the
    process exceeds this time, it will be terminated.






notify_classes   (default: bounce,defer,delay,enqueue,error,filter,forward)


A comma-separated list of message classes for which Postfix should
    generate notifications. These classes represent different delivery statuses or
    events.


For example, if bounce is listed, Postfix
    will send a bounce notification when a message cannot be delivered.






ntpd_enable   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will attempt to use
    NTP (Network Time Protocol) to synchronize its clock with a time server. This
    is important for accurate timestamping of mail headers and logs.






ntpd_host   (default: pool.ntp.org)


The hostname or IP address of the NTP server to use for time
    synchronization when ntpd_enable is enabled.






ntpd_port   (default: 123)


The UDP port number used for NTP communication. The default is 123,
    which is the standard NTP port.






ntpd_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for NTP requests. If the NTP server does not
    respond within this time, the time synchronization attempt will fail.






outbound_rate_delay   (default: 0s)


The delay introduced between sending individual messages to external
    destinations. A non-zero value rate-limits outgoing mail, typically to one
    message per specified interval. This can be useful for preventing mail
    servers from being blacklisted due to aggressive sending.


Specify a time value (e.g., 1s, 5m, 1h).


Note: The delay is enforced by the queue manager. The delay timer
    state does not survive "postfix reload" or "postfix stop".






owner_recursive_dirs   (default: 0o755)


The permissions for recursively created directories owned by the mail
    system user. This ensures that mail directories have appropriate access
    permissions.






owner_recursive_files   (default: 0o644)


The permissions for recursively created files owned by the mail system
    user. This ensures that mail files have appropriate access permissions.






parent_domain_matches_subdomains   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will consider a
    parent domain to match its subdomains when performing address lookups. For
    example, if example.com is listed in
    destinations, then
    mail.example.com will also be considered a local
    destination.


This behavior can be controlled by prepending a dot (.)
    to the domain name in the destinations or
    local_domain_maps parameters.






passive_expansion_limit   (default: 1000)


The maximum number of recipients that Postfix will expand from a
    distribution list or alias expansion during passive queue scans. This limits
    the number of recipients that Postfix will process without an active SMTP
    session, helping to prevent resource exhaustion.






passive_recipient_limit   (default: 50)


The maximum number of recipients Postfix will process per message during
    passive queue scans. This limits the number of recipients that Postfix will
    consider without an active SMTP session, helping to prevent resource
    exhaustion.






perl_busy_time_limit   (default: 300s)


The maximum time a Perl-powered content filter or milter is allowed to
    run before Postfix considers it busy and potentially times it out. This
    prevents runaway scripts from blocking mail processing.


This parameter affects Postfix integrations with Perl-based filters or
    milters.






perl_eval_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for evaluating Perl code within Postfix. This is
    used when Postfix executes Perl scripts for content filtering or other
    customizations. If the script execution exceeds this time, it will be
    terminated.






perl_init_timeout   (default: 30s)


The timeout duration for initializing the Perl interpreter within
    Postfix. This is relevant when Postfix integrates with Perl modules or scripts
    for mail processing.






pipe_append_at_sign   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will append an '@'
    sign to the recipient address when piping mail to an external command using the
    pipe(8) delivery agent. This is sometimes
    required by older or non-standard command-line mail utilities.






pipe_command_timeout   (default: 1000s)


The maximum time (in seconds) that a command executed by the pipe(8)
    delivery agent is allowed to run. If the command exceeds this limit, it will be
    terminated, and the delivery will be deferred.






pipe_environment   (default: empty)


A list of environment variables that should be passed to commands
    executed by the pipe(8) delivery agent. This
    allows customization of the execution environment for external commands.






pipe_filter_allow_unmatched   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will allow messages
    to pass through the pipe filter even if no matching rule is found. This can
    be useful for testing or for scenarios where only specific messages need to
    be filtered.






pipe_filter_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a message due to a pipe filter
    rule. The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.






pipe_filter_reject_text   (default: Message rejected by pipe filter)


The text message used when rejecting a message due to a pipe filter
    rule. The default is "Message rejected by pipe filter".






pipe_filter_table   (default: empty)


Specifies a lookup table for filtering messages processed by the
    pipe(8) delivery agent. This allows you to
    define rules that match specific message content or headers and take actions
    such as rejecting or discarding the message.


The format is similar to header_checks.






pipe_filter_verbose   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will log detailed
    information about the matching process for
    pipe_filter_table. This can be useful for
    debugging.






pipe_service_name   (default: pipe)


The name of the service in master.cf that handles pipe deliveries. The
    default is pipe.






postmaster_address   (default: $double_bounce_recipient)


The address of the postmaster for the local domain. This address is
    used for various administrative notices, including error reports and bounce
    messages. By default, it is set to the value of
    double_bounce_recipient.






postscreen_access_list   (default: permit_mynetworks,permit_sasl_authenticated,defer_all_mail)


A list of access control entries that define which clients are allowed
    to proceed past the Postscreen screening stage. The default allows clients
    from trusted networks, authenticated clients, and defers all others.


Entries can include:


    
  
  • permit_mynetworks: Allow clients from networks
      defined in mynetworks.
    • 
  
  • permit_sasl_authenticated: Allow clients that have
      successfully authenticated via SASL.
    • 
  
  • defer_all_mail: Defer all other clients.
    • 
  
  • IP addresses or CIDR blocks.
    • 
  
  • Lookup tables (e.g., hash:/etc/postfix/postscreen_access).
    • 



This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_allow_dequoted_literals   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will allow
    dequoted literal addresses in SMTP commands. This may be necessary for some
    older or non-compliant MTAs, but can also increase the risk of certain
    attacks.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_antispoof_enable   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will perform
    anti-spoofing checks, such as verifying reverse DNS records for connecting
    clients. This helps to prevent mail originating from forged IP addresses.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_assp_threshold   (default: 5)


The number of SMTP connection attempts from the same IP address within
    a short time that will trigger the ASSP (Anti-Spam SMTP Proxy) action. This
    is used in conjunction with the postscreen_dnsbl_action
    parameter.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_auth_username_length_limit   (default: 256)


The maximum length of a username allowed in SASL authentication credentials
    when processed by Postscreen. This is a security measure to prevent buffer
    overflows.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_bare_newline_enable   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will reject mail
    from clients that send bare newline characters in the SMTP protocol. Bare
    newlines are non-standard and can be used in certain types of attacks.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_bare_newline_action   (default: reject)


The action to take when a client sends bare newline characters. Possible
    values are reject (default) or
    log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_blacklist_action   (default: reject)


The action to take when a client is found in a blacklist (e.g., DNSBL).
    Possible values are reject (default) or
    log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_blind_RCPT_TO_enable   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will use blind
    RCPT TO commands to test recipient validity before accepting mail. This helps
    to prevent directory harvesting attacks.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_blind_RCPT_TO_log   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will log information
    about blind RCPT TO commands. This can be useful for debugging.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_blind_RCPT_TO_maxfailed   (default: 3)


The maximum number of failed blind RCPT TO commands allowed from a
    client before Postscreen takes action (e.g., rejects mail or defers
    connections).


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_cache_cleanup_interval   (default: 1h)


The interval at which Postscreen cleans up its internal cache of
    client information. This helps to prevent the cache from growing indefinitely.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_cache_count_limit   (default: 1000000)


The maximum number of entries allowed in the Postscreen cache. This
    limits the memory usage of the cache.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_cache_directory   (default: /var/lib/postscreen)


The directory where Postscreen stores its cache files. This cache
    stores information about clients that have been screened, allowing Postfix to
    make faster decisions on subsequent connections.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_cache_size_limit   (default: 10000000)


The maximum size (in bytes) of the Postscreen cache files. This limits
    the disk space used by the cache.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_cert_table   (default: empty)


A lookup table that specifies SSL/TLS certificates to be used for
    Postscreen's SMTP server. This is typically used when Postscreen needs to
    present a certificate to clients.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_cleanup_interval   (default: 1h)


The interval at which Postscreen performs cleanup tasks, such as
    removing old entries from its internal tables. This helps maintain performance
    and prevent resource leaks.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_client_dnsbl_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take when a client is found in a DNSBL during the client
    screening phase. Possible actions include dunno (no
    action), reject, or log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_client_dnsbl_lookup_domains   (default: empty)


A list of DNSBL domains to query for client IP addresses during the
    client screening phase. For example:


postscreen_client_dnsbl_lookup_domains = zen.spamhaus.org, bl.spamcop.net



This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_client_lookup_action   (default: DUNNO)


The action to take based on client IP address lookups (e.g., reverse
    DNS). Possible actions are DUNNO (no action),
    REJECT, or LOG.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_client_lookup_table   (default: empty)


A lookup table that defines actions based on client IP addresses. This
    allows for fine-grained control over which clients are allowed or rejected
    before the full SMTP transaction begins.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_client_master_service_list   (default: smtpd)


A comma-separated list of master service names that Postscreen uses to
    process client connections. The default is smtpd.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_client_rate_limit   (default: 100)


The maximum number of connections allowed from a single IP address within
    a specified time period. This helps to mitigate denial-of-service attacks.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_client_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a client based on Postscreen
    rules. The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_client_reject_text   (default: Client access denied)


The text message used when rejecting a client based on Postscreen
    rules. The default is "Client access denied".


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take when a client is found in a DNSBL during the mail
    screening phase. Possible actions include dunno (no
    action), reject, log, or
    templatetext.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_lookup_domains   (default: empty)


A list of DNSBL domains to query for sender IP addresses during the mail
    screening phase. For example:


postscreen_dnsbl_lookup_domains = zen.spamhaus.org, bl.spamcop.net



This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_mail_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take when a sender's IP address is found in a DNSBL. This
    is an alternative to postscreen_dnsbl_action
    and may apply different rules.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_mail_lookup_domains   (default: empty)


A list of DNSBL domains to query for sender IP addresses during the mail
    screening phase. This is an alternative to
    postscreen_dnsbl_lookup_domains
    and may apply different rules.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting mail due to a DNSBL listing. The
    default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_reject_text   (default: Sender IP listed)


The text message used when rejecting mail due to a DNSBL listing. The
    default is "Sender IP listed".


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_template_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting mail due to a DNSBL listing,
    using a template. This allows for more dynamic rejection messages.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_template_reject_text   (default: Sender IP listed in DNSBL)


The text message used when rejecting mail due to a DNSBL listing, using
    a template. This allows for more dynamic rejection messages.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_domain_lookup_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take based on domain lookups (e.g., reverse DNS of the
    sender's IP). Possible actions are dunno (no
    action), reject, or log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_domain_lookup_table   (default: empty)


A lookup table that defines actions based on domain lookups. This allows
    for fine-grained control over which domains are allowed or rejected.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_domain_lookup_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for domain lookups performed by Postscreen. If a
    lookup exceeds this time, it will be considered a failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_double_bounce_recipient   (default: postmaster)


The recipient address for double bounce messages generated by Postscreen.
    A double bounce occurs when an error notification message itself cannot be
    delivered.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dnsbl_dns_lookup_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for DNSBL lookups performed by Postscreen. If a
    DNSBL query exceeds this time, it will be considered a failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_dns_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for general DNS lookups performed by Postscreen.
    This applies to various DNS queries, not just DNSBL lookups.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_error_delay   (default: 5s)


The delay introduced after Postscreen encounters an error during client
    or mail screening. This helps to prevent rapid retries that could overwhelm
    the server or external services.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_exponential_backoff   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will use exponential
    backoff for retrying failed DNSBL lookups or other temporary errors. This
    means the delay between retries increases with each failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_fingerprint_lookup_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take when a fingerprint lookup fails. Fingerprint lookups
    are used to identify mail servers based on their IP addresses. Possible actions
    are dunno (no action), reject,
    or log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_fingerprint_lookup_domains   (default: empty)


A list of domains to query for fingerprint lookups. These are typically
    databases that map IP addresses to known mail server identities.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_fingerprint_lookup_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for fingerprint lookups performed by Postscreen. If
    a lookup exceeds this time, it will be considered a failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take based on the SMTP greeting banner from a client. This
    can be used to filter mail based on the banner's content. Possible actions are
    dunno (no action), reject,
    or log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_banner_lookup_table   (default: empty)


A lookup table that defines actions based on the SMTP greeting banner.
    This allows for fine-grained control over which greetings are accepted or
    rejected.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_command_time_limit   (default: 0s)


The time limit allowed for Postscreen to process the SMTP greeting and
    initial commands. If this time is exceeded, the connection will be dropped. A
    value of 0s means no limit.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_log   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will log information
    about SMTP greeting banners. This can be useful for debugging.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_master_service_list   (default: smtpd)


A comma-separated list of master service names that Postscreen uses to
    process greeting commands. The default is smtpd.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_rcpt_command_time_limit   (default: 0s)


The time limit allowed for Postscreen to process the RCPT TO command
    after the greeting. If this time is exceeded, the connection will be dropped. A
    value of 0s means no limit.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a connection based on the SMTP
    greeting. The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_reject_text   (default: Greeting rejected)


The text message used when rejecting a connection based on the SMTP
    greeting. The default is "Greeting rejected".


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_skip   (default: empty)


A list of IP addresses or networks that Postscreen should skip greeting
    checks for. This is typically used for trusted clients or internal servers.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_greet_time_limit   (default: 0s)


The time limit allowed for Postscreen to process the SMTP greeting. If
    this time is exceeded, the connection will be dropped. A value of 0s means no
    limit.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_ipv4_addresses_enable   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will perform screening
    checks on IPv4 addresses. This is the default behavior.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_ipv6_addresses_enable   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will perform screening
    checks on IPv6 addresses. This is the default behavior.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_log_key   (default: empty)


A string used as a key in Postscreen log messages. This can help to
    correlate log entries from different Postscreen processes.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_master_service_list   (default: smtpd)


A comma-separated list of master service names that Postscreen uses to
    process connections. The default is smtpd.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_cache_entries   (default: 1000000)


The maximum number of entries allowed in the Postscreen cache. This is a
    synonym for postscreen_cache_count_limit.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_cache_size   (default: 10000000)


The maximum size (in bytes) of the Postscreen cache files. This is a
    synonym for postscreen_cache_size_limit.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_connection_count   (default: 1000)


The maximum number of simultaneous connections allowed to the Postscreen
    daemon. This helps to prevent denial-of-service attacks.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_idle_time   (default: 300s)


The maximum time a Postscreen worker process will remain idle before
    exiting. This helps to manage system resources.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_idle_time_daemon   (default: 300s)


The maximum time the main Postscreen daemon process will remain idle
    before exiting. This helps to manage system resources.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_parallel_dnsbl   (default: 3)


The maximum number of parallel DNSBL lookups Postscreen will perform for a
    single client. This helps to prevent overwhelming DNSBL servers.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_parallel_dnsbl_domains   (default: 10)


The maximum number of parallel DNSBL lookups Postscreen will perform for
    a single client across all configured DNSBL domains. This is an overall limit
    on parallel DNS queries.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_parallel_jobs   (default: 1000)


The maximum number of parallel Postscreen jobs (connections) that can be
    handled simultaneously. This limits the load on the Postscreen daemon.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_max_use   (default: 100000)


The maximum number of times a Postscreen worker process will be reused
    before it is replaced. This helps to prevent resource leaks or memory
    fragmentation.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a connection or message by Postscreen.
    The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_reject_text   (default: Access denied)


The text message used when rejecting a connection or message by Postscreen.
    The default is "Access denied".


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_reject_log   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will log information
    about rejected connections or messages. This can be useful for debugging.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_sasl_auth_username_length_limit   (default: 256)


The maximum length of a username allowed in SASL authentication credentials
    when processed by Postscreen. This is a security measure to prevent buffer
    overflows. It is a synonym for
    postscreen_auth_username_length_limit.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_scan_after_sendbuf   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will perform mail
    screening checks after the entire message has been sent by the client. This
    allows for content-based filtering after the transmission is complete.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_scan_after_sendbuf_action   (default: reject)


The action to take when Postscreen finds a violation during the scan
    after sendbuf phase. Possible values are reject or
    log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_scan_after_sendbuf_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting mail due to a violation found
    during the scan after sendbuf phase. The default is 550, indicating a
    permanent failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_scan_after_sendbuf_reject_text   (default: Message rejected after sendbuf)


The text message used when rejecting mail due to a violation found
    during the scan after sendbuf phase. The default is "Message rejected after
    sendbuf".


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_sender_dnsbl_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take when a sender's IP address is found in a DNSBL during
    the mail screening phase. Possible actions include dunno
    (no action), reject, or log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_sender_dnsbl_lookup_domains   (default: empty)


A list of DNSBL domains to query for sender IP addresses during the mail
    screening phase. This is an alternative to
    postscreen_dnsbl_lookup_domains
    and may apply different rules.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_sender_lookup_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take based on sender IP address lookups (e.g., reverse
    DNS). Possible actions are dunno (no action),
    reject, or log.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_sender_lookup_table   (default: empty)


A lookup table that defines actions based on sender IP addresses. This
    allows for fine-grained control over which senders are allowed or rejected.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_sender_lookup_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for sender IP address lookups performed by Postscreen.
    If a lookup exceeds this time, it will be considered a failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_service_name   (default: postscreen)


The name of the Postscreen service as registered in the master.cf file.
    This is used internally by Postfix to manage the Postscreen daemon.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_skip_access   (default: empty)


A list of IP addresses, networks, or hostnames that Postscreen should
    skip screening for. This is typically used for trusted mail servers or internal
    clients.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_skip_cleanup   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will skip its
    periodic cleanup tasks. This is generally not recommended as it can lead to
    unbounded cache growth.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_skip_connection   (default: empty)


A list of IP addresses, networks, or hostnames for which Postscreen should
    skip connection-level checks. This is typically used for trusted clients or
    internal servers.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_skip_greeting   (default: empty)


A list of IP addresses, networks, or hostnames for which Postscreen should
    skip greeting checks. This is typically used for trusted clients or internal
    servers.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_skip_mail   (default: empty)


A list of IP addresses, networks, or hostnames for which Postscreen should
    skip mail-level checks (e.g., DNSBL lookups). This is typically used for
    trusted clients or internal servers.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_skip_postmaster   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will not perform
    screening checks for mail addressed to the postmaster. This can be useful if
    postmaster addresses are used for legitimate mail relay or administrative
    purposes.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_sleep_time   (default: 1s)


The amount of time Postscreen pauses between processing connections. This
    can help to reduce the load on the system and prevent aggressive blocking.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_templates   (default: empty)


A lookup table that defines templates for rejection messages. This allows
    for more dynamic and informative rejection notices based on the reason for
    rejection.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_template_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a message based on a template.
    The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_template_reject_text   (default: Access denied)


The text message used when rejecting a message based on a template. The
    default is "Access denied".


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_timeout   (default: 120s)


The total time limit for Postscreen screening. If a client connection
    exceeds this time, it will be disconnected.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_tls_security_level   (default: may)


The security level for TLS (Transport Layer Security) connections when
    Postscreen acts as an SMTP server. Possible values are:
    none (no TLS), may (TLS is
    optional), encrypt (TLS is required),
    verify (TLS is required and the client certificate is
    verified).


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_truncate_log   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will truncate its
    log file when it reaches a certain size. This prevents the log file from
    growing indefinitely.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_truncate_log_size   (default: 1000000)


The maximum size (in bytes) of the Postscreen log file before it is
    truncated, if postscreen_truncate_log
    is enabled.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_unknown_client_rcpt_to_defer   (default: 0s)


The delay introduced for unknown clients during the RCPT TO command
    processing. A non-zero value can help to slow down spambots that do not
    respect delays.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_unknown_client_rcpt_to_reject   (default: 0)


The number of unknown client RCPT TO commands allowed before rejection.
    A value greater than 0 enables rejection after that many attempts.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_unknown_client_rcpt_to_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting an unknown client during the RCPT
    TO command. The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_unknown_client_rcpt_to_reject_text   (default: Unknown recipient)


The text message used when rejecting an unknown client during the RCPT
    TO command. The default is "Unknown recipient".


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_unknown_client_rcpt_to_warn   (default: 0s)


The delay introduced for unknown clients during the RCPT TO command
    processing, specifically for logging warnings. A non-zero value can help to
    slow down spambots that do not respect delays.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_use_tls   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will attempt to
    establish a TLS connection when communicating with other Postfix daemons. This
    adds an extra layer of security for internal Postfix communication.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_verify_dnsbl_result   (default: yes)


If enabled (yes), Postscreen will verify the
    DNSBL lookup results by performing a reverse lookup. This helps to prevent
    DNSBL spoofing.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_verify_dnsbl_result_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for verifying DNSBL lookup results. If the reverse
    lookup exceeds this time, it will be considered a failure.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






postscreen_virtual_mailbox_maps   (default: empty)


A lookup table that defines virtual mailbox mappings for Postscreen. This
    allows Postscreen to apply different rules or actions based on virtual
    recipient addresses.


This parameter affects the postscreen(8)
    daemon.






proxy_dnsbl_action   (default: dunno)


The action to take when a proxy client is found in a DNSBL. Possible
    actions are dunno (no action), reject,
    or log.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






proxy_dnsbl_lookup_domains   (default: empty)


A list of DNSBL domains to query for proxy client IP addresses. For
    example:


proxy_dnsbl_lookup_domains = zen.spamhaus.org, bl.spamcop.net



This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






proxy_dnsbl_reject_code   (default: 550)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a proxy client due to a DNSBL
    listing. The default is 550, indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






proxy_dnsbl_reject_text   (default: Proxy client listed)


The text message used when rejecting a proxy client due to a DNSBL
    listing. The default is "Proxy client listed".


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






proxy_read_maps   (default: empty)


A list of lookup tables that the Postfix proxy service can read. This
    is used for services like proxy:passwd.byname to look
    up user information.






proxy_write_maps   (default: empty)


A list of lookup tables that the Postfix proxy service can write to. This
    is less commonly used and typically applies to specific database backends that
    support updates.






queue_directory   (default: /var/spool/postfix)


The main directory where Postfix stores its queue files (incoming, active,
    deferred, etc.).






queue_file_owner   (default: postfix)


The system user that owns the Postfix queue files. This is typically set
    to the user Postfix daemons run as (e.g., 'postfix').






queue_file_permissions   (default: 0600)


The permissions for the Postfix queue files. The default (0600) allows
    only the owner to read and write the file, which is a secure setting.






queue_id_length   (default: 8)


The length of the unique message identifier (queue ID) generated by Postfix.
    This ID is used in log messages and internal tracking.






queue_min_free   (default: 20MB)


The minimum amount of free disk space that Postfix requires in the
    queue_directory. If the available space drops
    below this limit, Postfix may stop accepting new mail or defer deliveries to
    prevent disk full errors.






queue_smtp_bounce_timeout   (default: 5s)


The time limit for the queue manager to process bounce messages generated
    by the SMTP client. This parameter is used internally by Postfix.






queue_smtp_defer_timeout   (default: 1s)


The time limit for the queue manager to process deferred messages generated
    by the SMTP client. This parameter is used internally by Postfix.






queue_smtp_filter_timeout   (default: 1s)


The time limit for the queue manager to process filtered messages generated
    by the SMTP client. This parameter is used internally by Postfix.






rate_limit_allow_unmatched   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will allow messages
    to bypass rate limiting if no matching rule is found in the rate limit table.
    This can be useful for testing or for scenarios where only specific messages
    need to be rate-limited.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






rate_limit_reject_code   (default: 451)


The SMTP reply code used when rejecting a message due to rate limiting.
    The default is 451, indicating a temporary failure.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






rate_limit_reject_text   (default: Too many connections)


The text message used when rejecting a message due to rate limiting. The
    default is "Too many connections".


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






rate_limit_table   (default: empty)


Specifies a lookup table for rate limiting incoming SMTP connections. This
    allows you to define rules that limit the number of connections or messages
    from specific IP addresses or networks within a given time frame.


The format of the table typically includes:


rate_time_interval:connection_count_limit



Example:
    10s:10  (Allow at most 10 connections per 10 seconds)


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






rate_limit_verbose   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will log detailed
    information about the matching process for rate_limit_table.
    This can be useful for debugging rate limiting rules.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






receive_override_send_skip   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will override the
    send skip setting when receiving mail. This means that messages will always be
    processed, even if they are marked to be skipped for sending.






receive_skip_verify_recipient   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will skip recipient
    verification when receiving mail. This can improve performance but may lead to
    mail being delivered to non-existent recipients.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






receive_skip_verify_sender   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will skip sender
    verification when receiving mail. This can improve performance but may lead to
    mail from forged senders being accepted.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






reject_code   (default: 550)


The default SMTP reply code used when rejecting a message for various
    reasons not specifically covered by other parameters. The default is 550,
    indicating a permanent failure.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






reject_message_domain   (default: empty)


A list of domains for which Postfix should reject all incoming mail. This
    is a simple way to block mail from specific domains.


Example:
    reject_message_domain = spam.com, malicious.org


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






reject_message_sender   (default: empty)


A list of sender addresses for which Postfix should reject all incoming
    mail. This is a simple way to block mail from specific senders.


Example:
    reject_message_sender = abuse@spam.com, blockme@malicious.org


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






reject_text   (default: Message rejected)


The default text message used when rejecting a message for various reasons
    not specifically covered by other parameters. This text is appended to the
    rejection code.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






relay_domains   (default: empty)


A list of domains for which this mail server is authorized to relay mail.
    If a message is for a domain listed here, Postfix will accept and forward it,
    even if the destination is not local. This is typically used for smarthosts
    or mail gateways.


If empty, only mail for local domains is accepted.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






relay_host   (default: empty)


Specifies a default smarthost for all outgoing mail. If this parameter is
    set, all mail not destined for a local domain will be sent to this relay host.
    This overrides the normal MX lookup process for non-local destinations.


Example:
    relay_host = smtp.example.com


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






relay_host_does_not_accept_local_recipient   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will assume that the
    relay_host does not accept mail for local
    recipients. This means that if the relay host is specified, Postfix will not
    attempt to deliver mail to local domains via that relay host.


This parameter affects the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.






relay_modules   (default: empty)


A list of modules that are loaded for relaying mail. This is typically
    used for advanced features or custom relaying mechanisms.






relay_recipient_maps   (default: empty)


A list of lookup tables that Postfix consults to determine if a recipient
    address is allowed for relaying. This allows for fine-grained control over
    which recipients can be relayed through the server.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server.






relay_transport   (default: smtp:$)'


The default message delivery transport for relayed recipients (i.e.,
    recipients not local to this server but for which this server is authorized
    to relay). This parameter specifies the entry in the master.cf file that
    Postfix should use. The default is the smtp(8)
    delivery agent.


This parameter affects the smtpd(8)
    server and the queue manager.






resolve_dequoted_addresses   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will attempt to resolve
    dequoted email addresses. This is typically used in conjunction with specific
    address rewriting or mapping schemes.






resolve_numeric_pivot   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will attempt to resolve
    numeric IP addresses in pivot tables. This is a rare configuration and usually
    not needed.






resolve_numeric_tables   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will attempt to resolve
    numeric IP addresses in lookup tables. This is a rare configuration and usually
    not needed.






resolver_delay_stats   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will collect statistics
    on DNS lookup delays. This can be useful for performance tuning and identifying
    slow DNS servers.






resolver_default_transport   (default: smtp)


The default delivery transport to use when Postfix cannot determine the
    appropriate transport via DNS lookups (e.g., MX records). The default is
    smtp.






resolver_loop_count_limit   (default: 100)


The maximum number of DNS lookup loops (e.g., CNAME chains) allowed for a
    single query. This prevents infinite loops in DNS resolution.






resolver_max_tries   (default: 3)


The maximum number of times Postfix will attempt to resolve a domain name
    or MX record. If all attempts fail, the lookup is considered unsuccessful.






resolver_prefer_ipv4   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will prefer IPv4
    addresses over IPv6 addresses when performing DNS lookups. This can be useful
    in environments where IPv6 connectivity is unreliable or not fully supported.






resolver_prefer_ipv6   (default: no)


If enabled (yes), Postfix will prefer IPv6
    addresses over IPv4 addresses when performing DNS lookups. This is the default
    behavior if the system supports IPv6.






resolver_query_timeout   (default: 10s)


The timeout duration for each individual DNS query attempt. If a DNS
    server does not respond within this time, Postfix will try another server or
    consider the query failed.






resolver_retransmissions   (default: 3)


The number of times Postfix will retransmit a DNS query to a specific
    server before giving up on that server. This is related to
    resolver_max_tries but applies to each
    individual server.






resolver_timeout   (default: 60s)


The total timeout duration for all DNS resolution attempts for a single
